output_template_per_job: Summary (generated; 80–110 characters; ends with a period; emphasize product development and technical execution)
Gestallt (separate section): 3 bullets (each 80–110 characters; emphasize user research, architecture decisions, HIPAA compliance, shipping)
CoverPro (separate section): 2 bullets (each 80–110 characters; emphasize problem identification, quality gates, automated systems)
Daylight (separate section): 2 bullets (each 80–110 characters; emphasize context recovery, multi-project management, automation)
labDemand: 1 bullet (80–110 characters; reframe for roadmap management across verticals; ends with a period)
Focus Digital: 2 bullets (each 80–110 characters; reframe for stakeholder communication and requirements gathering; no SEO metrics; ends with periods)
Lear Marketing: 1 bullet (80–110 characters; reframe for stakeholder presentations to non-marketing execs; ends with a period; no Toyota/eBay-specific claims)
WAR Cover Letter (separate document; NOT bound to 80–110 character lines)
NOTE: Do NOT output a separate 'Cover Letter (JD Questions Only)' section. If the JD asks questions, answer them under the WAR Cover Letter heading. Omit any section with no content.

resume_line_rules.punctuation: Summary and every bullet must end with a period.
resume_line_rules.truthfulness: Do not invent experience, employers, tools, titles, or results.
resume_line_rules.tailoring: Tailor bullets to each JD by reframing real experience, not by making new claims.

numbers_and_style.hard_rule: Do NOT spell out numbers to hit character limits (e.g., do not write 'two point four').
numbers_and_style.consistency: Keep number formats clean and recognizable; avoid gimmicks for length compliance.

gestallt_bullets: Emphasize: user research (SLPs, educators, families), architecture decisions (multi-tenant, RBAC, JWT), HIPAA compliance, shipping to production
Avoid: Low-level implementation details, technology bragging without outcome context
coverpro_bullets: Emphasize: problem identification (existing tools slow/expensive), quality gates (linter, similarity detection), automated systems (repair loops)
Avoid: AI buzzwords, over-technical descriptions of pipeline
daylight_bullets: Emphasize: context recovery architecture, multi-project management (17 repos), automation (staleness detection, blocker extraction)
Avoid: Personal workflow details, overly meta descriptions

focus_digital_pm_reframing.reframe_for: Stakeholder communication and requirements gathering, not SEO execution
allowed_angles: Requirements gathering from B2B clients (RF testing labs, industrial manufacturers)
Translating technical needs into deliverable outcomes
Managing roadmap across multiple client verticals
focus_digital_pm_reframing.forbidden: Do NOT include SEO metrics (+631% impressions, +366% traffic, etc.) in PM-focused resumes. Those belong in content strategist roles.

lear_marketing_pm_reframing.reframe_for: Stakeholder presentations and GTM strategy for technical products
allowed_angles: Presenting Ahrefs/SEMRush strategy to founders with no marketing background
Building modular systems for early-stage companies without marketing ops
Translating technical product capabilities into market positioning
lear_marketing_pm_reframing.no_toyota_or_ebay_claims: LM bullets cannot reference Toyota/eBay-specific bullets, outcomes, or brand claims.
lear_marketing_pm_reframing.allowed: General transferable skills and outcomes that are truly attributable to Lear Marketing work.

structure: Play 1: Address their top need with one of my strongest, most relevant strengths (win the round).
Play 2: Match a second need with another strength/experience (different angle, still relevant).
Play 3: Match a third need with a third strength/experience (show range and judgment).
Close: Direct call-to-action to schedule an interview; include risk-reversal cues (confidence without fluff).
writing_quality_expectations: Vary sentence structure; avoid repetitive 'Need identified → I solve it' loops.
Write with flow, persuasion, and empathy; concrete, human, non-generic.
No formatting constraints on the cover letter beyond topical fit and clarity.
pm_cover_letter_angles: Lead with shipped products (Gestallt, CoverPro, Daylight) as PM portfolio
Use marketing background to demonstrate stakeholder communication and requirements gathering
Emphasize full-stack execution (can write spec, build prototype, measure outcome)
Position as 'PM who can build' - eliminates PM→eng translation layer

quality_bar.tailor_per_jd: You cannot reuse identical project/marketing bullets across unrelated JDs.
quality_bar.reframing_allowed: You can reframe marketing work as PM skills (stakeholder communication, roadmap management, requirements gathering) without making anything up.
avoid_bad_habits: No half-true bullets padded by wordy workarounds.
No number spell-outs to game character limits.
No vague filler ('responsible for', 'worked on') when a stronger, truthful action exists.

bullet_count_target.rationale: This allocation fits on one page while leading with product work for PM roles.
